1.title: Cut off one clear plug
1.say: Lay the thick blue cable on the table. Snip off one clear plug close to the blue cover.
placements: clear plug on one end of thick blue cable → cut off and discard, leaving flat cut bare end on blue cable (in the video: blue coiled cable on black surface, then on brown table)
hand cutting tool → close around thick blue cable just behind clear plug to make the cut (in the video: yellow handled cutter on brown table)
watch_for: if both ends have no clear plug you cut both ends; use a new cable with one plug left.
if the blue cover is split far back you cut too far in; cut clean just behind the plug.
1.check_yourself: It should look like a coiled thick blue cable with one clear plug left and one flat blue cut end.
1.safety: Keep your fingers clear of the sharp cutting edge while you cut.

2.title: Peel back the outer blue cover
2.say: Hold the cut end steady. Peel back about one inch of the outer blue cover to show the small wires.
placements: outer blue cover at flat cut end → peel off about one inch to expose eight small coloured wires (in the video: cut end held over brown table)
hand stripping tool with yellow handles → set around cable about one inch from cut end and pull cover off (in the video: yellow handled tool centre of brown table)
watch_for: if the small coloured wires look nicked or cut you squeezed too hard; cut higher and strip again.
if less than a fingertip of colour shows you removed too little; strip a little more cover.
2.check_yourself: It should look like eight small coloured wires sticking out about one inch from the thick blue cable.
2.safety: Keep your fingertips away from the sharp edges and squeeze gently.

3.title: Untwist and straighten small wires
3.say: Spread the eight small wires apart with your fingers. Pull each twist open until every little wire lies flat and straight.
placements: small white string among wires → snip off at blue cover edge and pull out (in the video: white thread with twisted colours on brown table)
eight small twisted coloured wires → separate with fingers, untwist and pull straight to fan out (in the video: held between fingers with orange handled tool behind)
watch_for: if any pair still twists together the plug will fail; you should see eight separate straight wires.
if a little wire breaks when you pull you pulled too hard; start higher and pull gently.
3.check_yourself: It should look like eight separate straight little wires fanning out from the blue cover with no twists.
3.safety: Keep the sharp tips away from your fingers and the little wires.

4.title: Slide on small blue cover
4.say: Pick up the small blue rubber cover. Slide it over the wire ends down onto the thick blue cable.
placements: small blue rubber cover → slide over exposed wire ends down onto thick blue cable and push away from ends (in the video: cover sitting loose below straight wires on brown table)
watch_for: if the cover will not go over later you forgot it; you must slide it on before the plug.
if the wide cup faces away from the wires turn it around; the cup must face the wire ends.
4.check_yourself: It should look like a small blue rubber cover sitting loose around the thick blue cable below the straight little wires.

5.title: Line up wires and trim even
5.say: Lay the eight little wires flat side by side. Start with white with green stripes on the left and end with brown. Pinch them even and snip the ends straight across.
placements: white wire with green stripes → far left position 1 of row, leftmost (in the video: leftmost on fingertip, 568A position 1)
solid green wire → next to it position 2 (in the video: second from left on fingertip, 568A position 2)
white wire with orange stripes → middle left position 3 (in the video: third from left, 568A position 3)
solid blue wire → middle position 4 (in the video: fourth from left, 568A position 4)
white wire with blue stripes → middle position 5 (in the video: fifth from left, 568A position 5)
solid orange wire → middle right position 6 (in the video: sixth from left, 568A position 6)
white wire with brown stripes → next to it position 7 (in the video: seventh from left, 568A position 7)
solid brown wire → far right position 8 (in the video: rightmost on fingertip, 568A position 8)
uneven wire ends → trim straight across with cutter so all eight are same length to fit in plug (in the video: short even ends over brown table)
watch_for: if white with orange stripes is on the far left you mixed green and orange; far left must be white with green stripes.
if ends are uneven or splayed the plug will miss; all ends must line flat and even.
5.check_yourself: It should look like eight flat straight little wires side by side starting with white with green stripes and ending with brown and all cut even.
5.safety: Keep your fingers behind the sharp edges while you snip.

6.title: Push wires into clear plug
6.say: Hold the clear plug with the opening facing the wires. Push the eight flat wires far into the back until they touch the front.
placements: eight flat wires in green first order → push into back opening of clear plug until ends touch front and colours show at front (in the video: plug held in fingers over brown table)
thick blue cable outer cover → keep just inside back of clear plug with small blue rubber cover still down on cable (in the video: blue cover edge at plug back)
watch_for: if the order flips while pushing the cable will fail; check white with green stripes is still on the left.
if colours do not reach the front you did not push far; push until ends touch the front.
6.check_yourself: It should look like a clear plug on the wire ends with all the little colours showing in a line right up at the front.

7.title: Squeeze the plug tight
7.say: Set the clear plug into the front slot of the big squeezing tool. Squeeze the orange handles firmly together to lock it.
placements: clear plug with wires inside → set fully into front slot of big black squeezing tool with orange handles (in the video: black tool with orange handles on brown table)
orange handles of squeezing tool → squeeze firmly together to press plug tight (in the video: handles closed over brown table)
watch_for: if the plug pulls off easily you did not squeeze hard enough; squeeze until tight.
if the blue cover hangs outside the plug you did not push in far; blue cover must be tucked inside.
7.check_yourself: It should look like the clear plug is flattened tight onto the wires with the thick blue cover tucked just inside the back.
7.safety: Keep your fingers out from between the squeezing handles as you close them.

8.title: Slide blue cover over plug
8.say: Hold the finished clear plug steady. Slide the small blue rubber cover up over the back of the plug.
placements: small blue rubber cover down on cable → slide up over back of clear plug until it covers the joint (in the video: cover pulled up over plug back on brown table)
watch_for: if a gap shows between cover and plug you did not push up far; slide until it hugs.
if wires pull out while sliding hold the plug steady; colours must still show at front.
8.check_yourself: It should look like the small blue cover hugs the back of the clear plug with no gap.
